FORCE_UI_CHOICE.problem: Orient people within SF while comparing all-weather neighborhood point forecasts and independent beach conditions
FORCE_UI_CHOICE.goal: Preserve SD beach finder map materials; show materially different complete systems before choosing one
FORCE_UI_CHOICE.score_scale: 1 weak to 5 strong; max 20. Scores are design judgments, not user-study measurements.

matrix.label: Parks are the structure
matrix.rationale: Strong west / center / south anchors; weaker eastern address context.

matrix.label: A few streets, well chosen
matrix.rationale: Corridors explain journeys; needs real road geometry for production.

matrix.label: Recognize the skyline
matrix.rationale: Visitor recognition; more icon vocabulary and less neighborhood precision.

matrix.label: Parks + three corridors
matrix.rationale: Most complete SF frame while preserving quiet SD map materials.

matrix.label: Highways alone
matrix.rationale: Sparse SF central and western orientation; SD mechanism does not transfer alone.

matrix.label: Every neighborhood outlined
matrix.rationale: Existing names do not align with public polygons; implies false region precision.

matrix.label: Full local street atlas
matrix.rationale: Street texture overwhelms the weather and needs a zoom-dependent label engine.

matrix.label: Tourist symbols everywhere
matrix.rationale: Icon collisions with sky, beach and location semantics.

matrix.label: Continuous temperature surface
matrix.rationale: Requires interpolation and uncertainty absent from the current point model.

matrix.label: Radar-first orientation
matrix.rationale: Precipitation-specific; does not satisfy all-weather orientation.

matrix.label: 3D terrain and buildings
matrix.rationale: Adds implementation weight and perspective-dependent label comparison.

matrix.label: Transit skeleton
matrix.rationale: Useful for some journeys but uneven citywide and coastal context.

FORCE_UI_CHOICE.diversity_check: Park area structure, sparse street network, recognizable point landmarks, and a strictly budgeted hybrid differ in orientation grammar, hierarchy, density and audience; not palette swaps.

recommendation.why: Covers west, center, waterfront and south with a restrained map language.
recommendation.what_would_change_it: Driving-first use favors streets; visitor-first use favors landmarks; repeated metric comparison favors uniform information.

CHOICE_DISPLAY.mode: Responsive component grid switching to horizontal carousel above half-viewport height

chapters.title: How do you recognize SF?
chapters.intro: Four complete systems, on the same geography and weather. These change what the base map teaches you, not the forecast values.

chapters.title: What does one region look like?
chapters.intro: Same point coordinates and values; four different containers. Select a region on the large map to compare its expanded state.

options.title: A small weather ticket
options.description: Name, condition icon and temperature are always visible. One short line appears only when the information pattern calls for it.
options.benefit: Strong reading order; holds a missing value or an important exception naturally.
options.cost: Uses more area than a dot or chip. Needs collision handling before production.
options.mobile: Keep four representative tickets plus the selected point; all ten remain in the picker.

options.title: One-line label
options.description: Neighborhood name, condition and temperature share a compact capsule. Extra facts move to the selection dock.
options.benefit: The geography remains legible and labels feel close to the SD map.
options.cost: Cannot carry all exceptions. A map-wide notice and selected detail must preserve important missing or stale status.
options.mobile: The capsule stacks to avoid tiny text; selected detail remains below the map.

options.title: A two-reading strip
options.description: Neighborhood name sits above a compact row: condition, temperature and wind. A third line is available for a rain or UV exception.
options.benefit: Wind is comparable without opening every region.
options.cost: Ten labels become crowded; this is the densest option and the first one to fail on a phone.
options.mobile: Show only four representative strips. Do not shrink ten strips to fit.

options.title: Type directly on the map
options.description: Region name, icon and temperature sit on the land with a light text halo. Selection gets a solid backing.
options.benefit: The map feels continuous and generous.
options.cost: Legibility changes over roads, parks and coastline; important text needs a real backing.
options.mobile: A selected label becomes a ticket. Avoid stacking bare text over beach names.

chapters.title: What deserves map space?
chapters.intro: Every point keeps a temperature and a name unless the quiet pattern deliberately withholds the name. Additional fields answer a specific comparison question.

options.title: Shared core, local exceptions
options.description: Show name, sky and temperature everywhere. Add one line for rain, exposed wind, high UV, fog or missing evidence only where it matters.
options.benefit: Communicates SF’s differences while keeping most labels quiet.
options.cost: You cannot assume an absent wind line means no wind. The legend and selected dock must explain the hierarchy.
options.mobile: Show the strongest exception at each visible point; never suppress missing-data status.

options.title: The same three facts everywhere
options.description: Every ticket gets temperature, wind and UV, regardless of significance. The selection dock adds rain and timing.
options.benefit: Stable spatial memory: the same field is in the same place at every point.
options.cost: Dense even on a benign day. Equal visual weight makes important changes harder to spot.
options.mobile: Representative regions only, with an optional accessible list for all ten.

options.title: One question at a time
options.description: Choose a metric and promote it to the large number at every point. Here the initial lens is wind; the inspector also offers UV and rain chance.
options.benefit: The cleanest answer to “where is it less windy?” without ten full dashboards.
options.cost: A large 19 can be mistaken for temperature. Units and a persistent lens label are mandatory.
options.mobile: A sticky metric selector sits above the map; no unlabeled color scale.

options.title: Tell me what changes
options.description: The second line is a short temporal statement: fog until 2, rain arriving, wind after 3, sunny through 4.
options.benefit: Makes a weather map useful for planning, not just observing.
options.cost: Needs a real forecast-derived rule and a time window. Do not generate confident prose from sparse data.
options.mobile: One concise time phrase; open the dock for the hourly sequence.

options.title: Numbers first; detail on selection
options.description: All points retain temperature. The selected point gets a named ticket; the four mobile representatives retain enough context to be chosen.
options.benefit: Makes the microclimate contrast obvious with very little ink.
options.cost: Poor discoverability for users who do not know neighborhood geography. Not a strong first-visit default.
options.mobile: Pair with the named region picker; never rely on hover.

chapters.title: Put the system under pressure
chapters.intro: These are authored fixtures, not live forecasts or calibrated weather simulations. Each state applies to the complete SF map.

options.title: Marine layer, sunny Mission
options.description: Fog and stronger wind on the west; warmer sun in the Mission. Different regions earn different secondary facts.
options.benefit: Tests the reason to have a regional map at all.
options.cost: A point forecast does not define the edge of the fog.

options.title: The whole city clears
options.description: Temperatures increase, coastal fog icons disappear and rain chances become zero in this fixture.
options.benefit: Tests whether the default stays calm when there is little to warn about.
options.cost: Do not invent an attention-grabbing exception just to fill every label.

options.title: Rain arrives from the west
options.description: Rain chances are higher on the coast. Beach markers switch to a separate runoff-concern state.
options.benefit: Shows that rain affects both regional planning and beach evidence, through separate rules.
options.cost: A rain probability is not a rainfall total or a measured runoff advisory.

options.title: Windy coast, sheltered inland
options.description: Exposed points get larger wind values and gust text; the base map still has no fake continuous wind field.
options.benefit: Tests label capacity and the wind lens.
options.cost: A “gust” must be modeled or observed as a gust; not derived by adding ten in production.

options.title: A high-UV afternoon
options.description: UV rises to 8 in the east and 5 in the west. Sky icons alone would not communicate the difference.
options.benefit: Tests whether UV is findable without making it a beach-only field.
options.cost: Requires modeled timestamp and basis: current hour vs daily maximum.

options.title: After dark
options.description: Cooler temperatures and moon icons replace the daytime emphasis; UV is zero in this fixture.
options.benefit: Tests whether irrelevant daytime metrics can recede.
options.cost: This is a subdued day palette, not a finished dark-mode proposal.

options.title: Only some fields arrive
options.description: Outer Richmond and Marina lose wind and UV. Aquatic Park has an unknown beach state.
options.benefit: Shows a partial forecast without discarding the useful temperature.
options.cost: The one-line chip cannot hold field-level absence. The banner and detail dock must carry it.

options.title: An older forecast remains
options.description: Values remain readable with a map-wide warning and visible age. “Now” is a requested time, not a freshness claim.
options.benefit: Avoids turning a failed refresh into an unexplained blank map.
options.cost: Actual age thresholds are a product choice, not settled by this mock.

options.title: First load
options.description: Location names stay in place while forecast numbers show a neutral loading state.
options.benefit: The layout is stable and the user can recognize the city immediately.
options.cost: A loading fixture is intentionally static. This mock does not fetch data.

options.title: Nothing could load
options.description: The map and names remain; values show dashes and an explicit error. Try again returns to the baseline fixture.
options.benefit: A recoverable state without replacing the entire map.
options.cost: Real retry would need per-source and per-point results.

chapters.title: Choose each icon independently
chapters.intro: All symbols are original SVGs with the same stroke weight. Select an option to see it at beaches, in the UV reading, on the simulated location, or in navigation.

options.title: Swimmer + condition badge
options.description: A swimmer says what the condition concerns; the small square, diamond or circle says which evidence state is active.
options.benefit: Most direct activity meaning. It stays distinct from generic water.
options.cost: Most detail at small sizes. Always pair the expanded state with a word.

options.title: Beach flag + condition badge
options.description: A flag is easy to recognize at the water and remains legible at 20 pixels.
options.benefit: Simple silhouette and easy active-state changes.
options.cost: Could imply an official lifeguard flag. Keep evidence text explicit.

options.title: Waves + condition badge
options.description: Three waves carry the beach layer, with a persistent status badge.
options.benefit: Clean and readable next to temperature.
options.cost: Could mean tide or surf rather than swimming. The legend must name the layer.

options.title: Sun + UV number
options.description: Use the sun only beside the written label “UV index” and its numeric value.
options.benefit: Immediate recognition and good size reduction.
options.cost: The same sun is also a sky condition. Context must distinguish them.

options.title: Lettered UV symbol
options.description: A purpose-made UV letterform with a baseline. The text label remains for accessibility.
options.benefit: No ambiguity with sunny weather.
options.cost: More typographic than pictographic. Test the small U / V separation.

options.title: Shade / umbrella symbol
options.description: An umbrella suggests shade as a response to UV exposure.
options.benefit: Connects the reading to an outdoor decision.
options.cost: An umbrella often means rain. Weakest standalone choice.

options.title: Blue dot with accuracy ring
options.description: A filled center and ring separate the user from hollow weather point markers. The mock location is simulated.
options.benefit: Familiar “you are here” convention.
options.cost: A real accuracy ring should represent GPS accuracy, not a decorative constant.

options.title: Crosshair
options.description: Use a target to recenter; the same symbol can mark the simulated user position for comparison.
options.benefit: Clear action meaning in a toolbar.
options.cost: As a map marker it can look like a selected forecast coordinate.

options.title: Heading arrow
options.description: A directional arrow points along a known device heading.
options.benefit: Helpful while walking and orienting the map.
options.cost: This north-facing demo is not a heading measurement. A real arrow needs permission and a useful heading.

options.title: Leave this frame
options.description: An arrow leaving a rectangle distinguishes opening the neighboring regional map from selecting a forecast point.
options.benefit: Conveys a change in geographic scope.
options.cost: Can also suggest sign-out. Always write “Marin” or “East Bay.”

options.title: Compass
options.description: A compass accompanies the destination name at map edges and in nearby comparison controls.
options.benefit: Suggests geographic exploration.
options.cost: Does not itself communicate the destination or the scope change.

options.title: Destination + chevron
options.description: A simple chevron relies on the written destination. Minimal and familiar.
options.benefit: Least visual noise inside a selected-region panel.
options.cost: Weak geographic meaning when shown without the destination.

chapters.title: Choices that change the product
chapters.intro: These choices affect what the map promises. Treat them separately from typography and icon taste.

options.title: The existing ten SF points
options.description: Use exactly the ten SF coordinates already configured in the app. The south and southeast remain visibly sparse.
options.benefit: Makes the first integration compatible with current data and region navigation.
options.cost: The picture is not comprehensive SF coverage. Empty space must not imply identical weather.

options.title: Six anchors + your selection
options.tag: An overview, not a new region model
options.description: Keep west-coast contrast, Marina, Market, Mission and Lake Merced. Retain a seventh ticket if the user selects another existing point.
options.benefit: Cuts clutter at the city scale without deleting any forecast location.
options.cost: Inner / Outer neighborhood comparisons need selection or a closer view.

options.title: Fourteen points across SF
options.description: Add proposed Noe Valley, Potrero Hill, Bayview and Excelsior coordinates to expose the coverage gap and label-density tradeoff.
options.benefit: Makes the southern and southeastern city part of the conversation.
options.cost: These four points and their weather are only proposals. Needs source-grid resolution and a stronger collision policy.

options.title: Forecast points
options.description: A visible dot anchors every ticket to one coordinate. No filled region claims uniform weather between points.
options.benefit: Matches the existing app’s location-based data model.
options.cost: “Region” is a navigation label, not an area measurement.

options.title: A soft selection area
options.description: A dashed, lightly filled ellipse around the selected forecast suggests the immediate vicinity without outlining neighborhoods.
options.benefit: Selection is easy to locate.
options.cost: A radius looks quantitative. Without a defined basis, this is a schematic selection aid only.

options.title: Neighborhood context outlines
options.description: Dashed public analysis-neighborhood boundaries provide orientation. Some do not match the app’s names, so they are not clickable forecast areas.
options.benefit: Shows the cost of adding area boundaries before a weather-region model exists.
options.cost: Can imply false precision and conflict with Inner / Outer Sunset or the Market Street point.

options.title: Independent named beach layer
options.description: Show four named beach points along the water, with a fixed list in the dock. These are not attached to weather regions.
options.benefit: A beach can be selected from any neighborhood.
options.cost: The northern waterfront needs careful label placement.

options.title: Symbols on map, names in dock
options.description: The same independent beach points remain, but their names live in the beach list and the opened detail.
options.benefit: Preserves the coastline and avoids cramming northern labels.
options.cost: One more interaction to identify an unfamiliar beach.

options.title: One suggested beach
options.description: Show one sample suggested beach for the selected weather point, keeping all beaches in the dock.
options.benefit: Cuts clutter and resembles the app’s current region-to-swim-spot shortcut.
options.cost: Hides nearby alternatives and reintroduces a relationship the geography may not justify.

options.title: A shared requested hour
options.description: Every point is compared at noon in the baseline. The selected dock previews the next few hours.
options.benefit: Same-time comparisons are interpretable.
options.cost: Must separately label forecast issuance and observations when connected.

options.title: One citywide time step
options.description: The whole map moves to 4 pm together. This fixture warms the coast slightly and cools the east slightly.
options.benefit: Lets you compare where to go later without changing ten region views.
options.cost: Hour changes need loading and freshness semantics for every field.

rejectedOverlays.reason: Ten full forecast cards overwhelm the geography.
Cannot identify neighborhoods or communicate a metric value.
Covers northern labels and prevents repeated multi-region comparison.
